admission.justification: Repeating an interrupted accepted pair must not create another code commit or abandon its memory attribution.

applicability: Exact retry or advertised public recovery of an accepted direct-create generation.
conditions: The persisted input fingerprint, code output and memory state are mechanically recoverable.
exclusions: Ambiguous or replaced code/ref/history states require the retained developer-decision path.
No new generation or second code commit is inferred from a cut.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_direct_landing.py::DirectLandingTests::test_public_recover_control_completes_cut_generation, test_moved_code_branch_keeps_generation_ambiguous; worker journal R4 section; R5 verdict 88c054160ffdffef415a01cdf0f09161bb59aa68944469379856e72944c46755

statement: An exact repeat of a mechanically recoverable create call resumes and completes its admitted generation with fingerprint, code commit and memory identity preserved, while a genuinely ambiguous moved-code cut stays in flight under an explicit developer-decision refusal.
